newsitem.title: UK: R-OPTIONS - Calls bought in British Gas.
newsitem.headline: R-OPTIONS - Calls bought in British Gas.

text.p: Calls were bought in British Gas Plc on Thursday, dealers said, as the underlying stock rose in heavy trading after a report in the Financial Times said major investment funds were underweight the stock.
With the shares rising 10p to 228-1/2 by 1450 GMT in volume of 9.6 million shares, volume in the December 240p calls rose to 1,035 lots.

Elsewhere in a relatively quiet options market, dealers highlighted a seller of the January 770p puts in National Westminster Bank Plc, where some 455 lots were traded. The underlying shares were up 10p at 676.
In B.A.T Industries Plc dealers highlighted a buyer of puts in the stock. In the January 420 puts volume reached 2,400 lots.
B.A.T calls were also active. In the April 550p calls, volume reached 1,000 and in the April 500p puts some 500 lots were dealt.
B.A.T shares were up 8p at 496-1/2 in heavy trade of 12.8 million shares amid continued demerger hopes and as some investors sought out stocks which have lagged the rest of the market this year.
Index options were relatively quiet after the active trading of earlier in the week sparked by volatility in the FTSE 100 and other leading markets.
"It has been one of those days where everyone is happy just to catch their breath," said one dealer.
